statement:
Design a key–value cache with a fixed capacity that evicts the **least recently used** entry when it overflows.

Implement the `LRUCache` class:
- `LRUCache(capacity)` sets the positive maximum number of entries.
- `get(key)` returns the value stored for `key`, or `-1` if the key is absent. A successful lookup counts as a use.
- `put(key, value)` inserts the pair or overwrites an existing key's value (also a use). If this pushes the number of keys above `capacity`, remove the key that has gone unused the longest.

Both `get` and `put` must run in `O(1)` average time.

examples.explanation: Reading key `1` makes key `2` the stalest, so inserting `3` evicts `2`. Inserting `4` then evicts `1`.
Overwriting key `1` updates its value without consuming extra capacity.

constraints: At most 2 × 10⁵ calls in total are made to get and put
hints: A hash map alone gives O(1) lookups but cannot tell you which key is least recently used; you also need an order that can be updated in O(1).
Pair the hash map with a doubly linked list ordered by recency, where the map stores each key's list node.
On every `get` hit or `put`, unlink the node and move it to the most-recent end; when the size exceeds `capacity`, remove the node at the least-recent end and delete its key from the map.

variants.title: Count LRU misses
variants.approach: Ordered hash map · O(1) per request
variants.statement: A cache holds at most `capacity` pages and evicts the **least recently used** page when full. Starting empty, the requests in `pages` are served in order; a request for a page not in the cache is a miss and loads it. Return the total number of misses.

examples.explanation: 1,2 miss; 1 hits; 3 misses and evicts 2; 2 misses again: 4 misses.

why.d: Checks `pages` where every value is the same.

hints: A hit refreshes the page's recency.
A doubly linked list plus hash map (or an ordered dict) gives O(1) move-to-front and evict.

why.d: Checks duplicate values in `pages` and 19 elements.
Checks duplicate values in `pages` and 15 elements.
Checks duplicate values in `pages` and 17 elements.
Checks the core logic on an ordinary input (4 elements) against the expected answer `4`.

solutions.name: Recency List Scan
solutions.description: Keep the cached pages in a list ordered from least to most recent; a hit is found by linear search and moved to the end, a miss evicts the front when full.

code.bash:
cacheMisses() {
    local capacity="$1" misses=0 p i found
    local -a pages cache  # cache: least recent first
    read -ra pages <<< "$2"
    for p in "${pages[@]}"; do
        found=-1
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#cache[@]}; i++ )); do
            if (( cache[i] == p )); then found=$i; break; fi
        done
        if (( found >= 0 )); then
            cache=("${cache[@]:0:found}" "${cache[@]:found+1}")  # remove it, re-append below
        else
            (( misses++ ))
            (( ${#cache[@]} == capacity )) && cache=("${cache[@]:1}")
        fi
        cache+=("$p")
    done
    echo "$misses"
}

solutions.name: Ordered Hash Map (Optimal)
solutions.description: A hash map combined with a recency-ordered linked list gives O(1) lookup, move-to-most-recent, and eviction of the least recent page.

code.bash:
cacheMisses() {
    local capacity="$1" misses=0 size=0 p old
    local -a pages
    read -ra pages <<< "$2"
    # ordered hash map: a doubly linked list threaded through two maps,
    # H (head sentinel, least recent) ... T (tail sentinel, most recent)
    local -A prev next
    next[H]=T; prev[T]=H

    unlink() { next[${prev[$1]}]=${next[$1]}; prev[${next[$1]}]=${prev[$1]}; unset "prev[$1]" "next[$1]"; }
    append() { prev[$1]=${prev[T]}; next[$1]=T; next[${prev[T]}]=$1; prev[T]=$1; }

    for p in "${pages[@]}"; do
        if [[ -n ${next[$p]} ]]; then  # hit: move to the most-recent end
            unlink "$p"; append "$p"
            continue
        fi
        (( misses++ ))
        if (( size == capacity )); then  # evict the least recently used
            old=${next[H]}; unlink "$old"; (( size-- ))
        fi
        append "$p"; (( size++ ))
    done
    echo "$misses"
}

variants.title: LFU eviction instead
variants.approach: Frequency buckets of ordered maps · O(1) per op
variants.statement:
Simulate a **least-frequently-used** cache of size `capacity`. Each op is `["get", key]` or `["put", key, value]`. Both a successful `get` and a `put` on an existing key increase that key's use count; a new key starts at count 1.

When inserting a new key into a full cache, evict the key with the **lowest use count**, breaking ties by the **least recently used**. Return the results of all `get` ops in order (`-1` for a miss).

examples.explanation: Key 2 has count 1 vs key 1's 2, so 2 is evicted.
Capacity 1: key 1 is evicted for key 2.

hints: Group keys by use count, and inside a group keep recency order.
Track the current minimum count; it resets to 1 on every new insertion.
When a key's count grows and its old bucket empties, bump the minimum if it was that bucket.

solutions.name: Scan for Victim
solutions.description: Store each key's value, use count and last-used tick; when a new key arrives in a full cache, scan every key for the lowest (count, tick).

code.python:
def lfuResults(capacity, ops):
    store = {}  # key -> [value, count, last_used]
    out, tick = [], 0
    for op in ops:
        tick += 1
        key = int(op[1])
        if op[0] == "get":
            if key in store:
                store[key][1] += 1
                store[key][2] = tick
                out.append(store[key][0])
            else:
                out.append(-1)
            continue
        value = int(op[2])
        if key in store:
            store[key][0] = value
            store[key][1] += 1
            store[key][2] = tick
            continue
        if len(store) == capacity:
            victim = min(store, key=lambda k: (store[k][1], store[k][2]))
            del store[victim]
        store[key] = [value, 1, tick]
    return out

solutions.name: Frequency Buckets (Optimal)
solutions.description: Group keys by use count, each group kept in recency order, and track the minimum count; eviction pops the oldest key of the minimum bucket.

solutions.description: Store values in a hash map and keep keys in an array ordered by use; touching a key moves it to the end and eviction removes the front.
keyPoints: Moving a key costs a linear removal

solutions.description: The map points each key at a node in a doubly linked list ordered by recency, so moving a node to the front and evicting from the back are both constant time.
keyPoints: Sentinel head and tail simplify edge cases
Most recent sits next to head
Evict the node just before tail
